candidates.name: Reuse one stateless encoder instead of constructing one per json() call
candidates.reason: Encoder construction is only 0.37% of json(), so the ceiling on this idea is 0.37% plus whatever attribute-lookup noise it removes -- measured at 1.69% and 0.20%, against a required 10%. Note it would have been SAFE: JSONContent is a cdef class with no instance state (no __dict__), so a shared instance is not the 'mutable encoder instance' the acceptance criteria warn about. It simply is not worth anything.

candidates.name: Skip dataclasses.asdict's recursive deep copy inside json()
candidates.reason: The intermediate dict json() builds is discarded immediately, so copying looks like pure waste -- but the copy is OBSERVABLE. A value with a custom __deepcopy__ has it invoked exactly once during json(), verified on BOTH builds. Skipping the copy would silently stop running user code. That is precisely the 'custom encoders, __deepcopy__ and exclusion/null side effects' the task requires be preserved.

characterized_quirks: json(**kwargs) silently IGNORES per-call options: kwargs are forwarded to the encoder's CONSTRUCTOR (self.__encoder__(**kwargs)), never to encode(). option=OPT_SORT_KEYS and indent=2 both have no effect and raise nothing. Verified identical on 0.10.21, so it is pre-existing, not a regression. Fixing it would be new JSON semantics, which spec section 1 puts out of scope, so it is pinned by test rather than corrected.
JSONContent has no instance state at all, which is why a shared encoder was even considered; a test now fails if instance state is ever added.

cold_vs_warm.note: Measured separately, as the task requires. Cold = first call on a freshly built instance; warm = steady state.

cost_breakdown.note: as_dict dominates. Any future serialization work should start there, not at the encoder -- but see the rejection reason for candidate B before trying.

headline: RETAIN THE CURRENT SERIALIZATION PATH. AC10 requires >=10% warm JSON improvement. The only SAFE candidate -- reusing one stateless encoder instead of constructing one per call -- measured +1.69% (Employee) and +0.20% (UnconstrainedScalars), because encoder construction is 0.37% of json(). The candidate that WOULD pay, skipping dataclasses.asdict's recursive deep copy at 76.8% of json(), is rejected on compatibility: a user's __deepcopy__ genuinely runs during json(), so removing the copy is an observable behaviour change. No production file was modified.
